subject: Clarify ML model-improvement exclusion and signature path for DPA
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clearwaterhealth.com>, Lori Jensen <lori.jensen@clearwaterhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify ML model-improvement exclusion and signature path for DPA

Olivia / Lori,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a clean set of redlines and a short summary that attempts to reconcile Clearwater's non-training requirement with how Redwood operates in production. High level proposal:

- Redwood will not use Customer Data (as defined below) to directly train or fine-tune model weights used in our public or hosted model catalog without an explicit, documented opt-in.
- We will retain the right to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and metrics for safety, reliability, and infrastructure optimizations (e.g., batching, KV-cache heuristics, prompt routing).
- "Model Improvement" is scoped to performance/ops telemetry and does NOT include training that produces customer-specific outputs or model derivatives tied to identifiable customer data.
- We propose a maximum raw data retention of 30 days for routing/debugging unless otherwise required for incident response/legal holds.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_v2_redlines.pdf and ML_Use_Definitions_Summary.docx with proposed definitions and a suggested signature path (DocuSign). If that looks reasonable, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope and route to your GC for final acceptance.

Would you be open to the above compromise (no training on Customer Data without opt-in; allow operational telemetry + de-id aggregate improvements)? If yes, we will update the DocuSign envelope and route for signatures.

Thanks,

--
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192


-----Original Message-----
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clearwaterhealth.com>
Sent: 2026-08-02T13:05:00-07:00
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lori Jensen <lori.jensen@clearwaterhealth.com>, Samuel Torres <s.torres@clearwaterhealth.com>
Subject: Re: Clarify ML model-improvement exclusion and signature path for DPA

David,

Thanks for the summary and the redlines. I shared these with our GC and security team — a couple of clarifications from our side:

- Clearwater requires an explicit opt-in for any training that results in model weight updates that could influence outputs. "De-identified aggregate telemetry" is acceptable but must be defined (no reconstruction of PII; enforceable de-identification standard).
- We need a clear subprocessors annex and the ability to approve changes to the subprocessor list for any processor that will see raw customer content.
- Cross-border transfers must be limited to locations listed in the DPA; any change requires prior notice and a right to object.

I've attached our annotated notes (see attached: Clearwater_DPA_comments.docx). Would you be able to call the proposed de-id standard out in the DPA (e.g., NIST- or ISO-based language) and confirm whether Redwood's telemetry pipeline can produce exportable evidence for audits?

Best,
Olivia

Olivia Park
Director, Information Security | Clearwater Health

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Sent: 2026-08-03T08:20:00-07:00
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clearwaterhealth.com>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Clarify ML model-improvement exclusion and signature path for DPA

Hi Olivia — looping Neha in from legal. Appreciate the specifics; I think we can get to a pragmatic agreement that protects Clearwater while allowing Redwood to maintain quality and safety:

- Proposed compromise language (for your legal review):
  * "Customer Data" means data provided to Redwood by or on behalf of the Customer under the Agreement. Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update model weights for commercial models without Customer's prior written consent.
  * "Operational Telemetry" (examples: latency metrics, tokenization errors, aggregate prompt-class histograms) may be used by Redwood for safety and performance improvements provided such telemetry is de-identified and cannot be traced back to Customer or individuals.
  * Redwood will provide a CSV export of telemetry summaries on request for audit (subject to redaction for other customers).
- We can agree to publish and maintain a Subprocessors Annex; Redwood commits to 30 days advanced notice of any new subprocessor plus an approval window for enterprise customers.

If that reads OK to you, we can take Neha's redline, incorporate your suggested de-id standard (NIST 800-188 or equivalent), and then prepare an envelope for DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that helps move this to signature.

-Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (617) 555-0123


-----Original Message-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Sent: 2026-08-03T12:10:00-07:00
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clearwaterhealth.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Clarify ML model-improvement exclusion and signature path for DPA

Olivia,

Thanks for your note. From a legal perspective, a few suggested edits and asks before we finalize:

1) Narrow but precise non-training clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to directly train, fine-tune or otherwise update model weights of general-purpose or customer-facing models without Customer's prior written consent. For clarity, Redwood may use de-identified or aggregated telemetry for operational improvements (not for creating model derivatives trained on Customer Data)."

2) Definition guidance: add explicit definitions for "de-identified" (reference to NIST guidelines), "derived data" and "model derivatives". Example snippet to put in the DPA: 

  "De-identified Data" means data which has been processed to remove or transform personal identifiers such that the likelihood of re-identification is remote and would require disproportionate effort. Redwood will apply industry-standard de-identification techniques (see NIST SP 800-188 or ISO 20889) and document the technique in an appendix upon request.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood will publish an up-to-date Subprocessors Annex and will provide 30 days' notice for changes. Clearwater shall have the right to object to a new subprocessor; if objection cannot be resolved within 15 days, Redwood shall either: (a) not engage the subprocessor for the affected customer's services, or (b) engage but provide reasonable compensating controls (e.g., dedicated tenancy, contractual controls).

4) Audit and evidence: Clearwater requests SOC 2 Type II report and periodic evidence of de-identification and retention practices. Redwood to provide SOC 2 and a one-time attestation on de-id techniques within 15 business days after the DPA is signed.

5) Cross-border transfers: scope transfers to approved regions; for other transfers, provide prior notice and Standard Contractual Clauses (or equivalent).

6) Execution: we can do DocuSign but would like a single mutual signature path (Redwood -> Clearwater GC -> Customer Exec). Please include the envelope link here when ready.

If these edits are acceptable, Neha will prepare a clean redline we can route for signature. I included a short redline snippet below for insertion into Section 2.1 (Data Use):

  "Except where Customer has expressly consented in writing, Processor shall not use Customer Data to directly train or adjust the weights of any machine learning model that may result in outputs influenced by Customer Data (\"Training\"). Processor may use De-identified Data and aggregate telemetry for the limited purposes of system performance, reliability, and safety provided such processing cannot be reasonably re-associated with Customer or an individual. Processor will document de-identification techniques and make them available under agreed confidentiality protections.

Happy to finalize — we want to get this on the books for the pilot.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
